name: Stable Unlabeled Complexity of Singletons
details: The value field includes the one-concept case. Reconstruction may be improper for $n\ge2$.
proof: For $n=1$, always reconstruct the sole concept from the empty key. For $n\ge2$, decode the empty key as the all-zero word and the coordinate key $\{i\}$ as singleton $\{i\}$. A realizable sample with a positive coordinate retains that coordinate; an all-negative sample retains nothing. This uses no retained label or side information. Every intermediate subsample containing the retained key still has that positive observation, or is again all-negative when the key is empty. Hence the key and reconstruction are stable. Two distinct full concepts forbid width zero. The empty-key output is improper for $n\ge2$.
